text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- The Mauerbach auction of Jewish art seized by the nazis started off successfully. The proceeds will go to Austrian Jewish victims of nazi repression.
- Government initiatives to help Austria's ailing construction industries have so far failed. New record highs in unemployment in the sector are expected.
- Trader and trade unions are against plans for longer shopping hours. Chamber of Economy chief Leopold Maderthaner expects the draft law not to pass through the parliament.

- Finance Minister Viktor Klima is preparing to work on governmental budgets for 1998 and 1999, so that discussions on the budget will not disturb Austria's presidency of the EU in the second half of 1997.
- Brewer Ottakringer has reported pre-tax losses of nine million schillings in the first half of 1996 compared to profits of 14 million the previous year due to lower exports and sales.
- German chemical giant Hoechst is closing down its unit Austria Faserwerke, which it only recently took over from fibre maker Lenzing.
- OMV is planning to invest 4.5 billion schillings over the next three years in its gas business.
- German tyre maker Continental is strengthening its Austrian unit Semperit in the lorry tyre business after halving car tyre production there.
- Austria is not working hard enough to keep its position in the emerging markets, Andreas Woergoetter of economic research institute IHS says.
- The government is looking at a new system of subsidies for Austrian tourism. In the future money may go to regions not municipalities.
- Austria will profit from EMU because of its strong connections abroad, analysts at Creditanstalt say.
